newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OECD says Austria needs extra budget efforts.
newsitem.headline: OECD says Austria needs extra budget efforts.

text.p: Austria will have to make extra efforts to keep its budget deficit under control in 1998, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said in a report released on Tuesday.

"The budget deficit is now projected to come in at three percent of gross domestic product (GDP)," the OECD said in a regular review of the country's economy. "Additional measures are necessary to prevent it rising again in 1998."

The OECD said it expected the country's 1998 deficit to come in at 3.4 percent, above the three percent target set by the Maastricht treaty on Europe's planned single currency. For the current year, it forecast a deficit of exactly three percent.

The organisation also revised its growth forecast for the Austrian economy up to 1.5 percent this year from a previous forecast of 1.4 percent, and to 2.4 percent in 1998 from an earlier estimate of 2.3 percent.

The report said a pickup in investment expenditures, fuelled by buoyant exports, was to a large extent outweighed by stagnant public and private consumption, caused by a fiscal consolidation of around one percent of GDP. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
